title: Fuzzy PI vs PI vs gain-scheduled PI on a nonlinear tank, matched tuning budget
algorithm: Mamdani fuzzy PI (incremental), PI, gain-scheduled PI; Nelder-Mead tuning

dataset.name: none
dataset.description: Simulated tank, illustrative parameters; Gaussian measurement noise in test B.

status.software: Executed from a clean kernel; local unit tests passed at build time; GitHub Actions has not been run on this repository

limitations: One plant, one rule base, one tuning algorithm; no statistical repeats over seeds for tuning.
Illustrative plant parameters; no measured data.
Local optimiser (Nelder-Mead) from a model-based start; a different start or budget could change the ranking.
GS-PI uses plant structure the other controllers do not.

checks.name: membership degrees sum to 1 on [-1,1] (partition of unity)
Phi(1,1) within 5e-3 of the closed-form centroid 8/9 on the default 201-point universe
Phi(1,1) converges to 8/9 when the universe is refined to 20001 points (error < 2e-4)
equivalent start: fuzzy and PI increments agree in the linear region (<2%)
local plant gain from simulation follows 2 sqrt(h)/c (nonlinear gain ratio 3 m vs 0.5 m)
same tuning budget: every controller used 100 to 104 objective evaluations
PI: tuned training cost <= starting cost
GS-PI: tuned training cost <= starting cost
Fuzzy PI: tuned training cost <= starting cost
PI: end-of-segment error below 3% of the largest step on test A (steady state reached)
GS-PI: end-of-segment error below 3% of the largest step on test A (steady state reached)
Fuzzy PI: end-of-segment error below 3% of the largest step on test A (steady state reached)
repeat tuning: all 15 repeat runs produced finite test costs
